families.name: F1 — results-summary-session-58 § 9: sweep argmax vote threshold misstated at its own era
families.mechanism: Document line 312-315 (unchanged since 69e9cf748, 2026-03-28) reads 'best F1 approx 0.552 at 5-of-10'. The anchor results/h11-384-single-pass-t0-rerun/consensus-analysis-report.json records $.optima.global_optimum = {pool_size: 10, threshold: 10, f1: 0.5521}. The sibling values in the same claim both MATCH (value_index 0, F1 0.5521; value_index 2, pool_size 10) — only the threshold numeral is wrong. The artefact's own full sweep puts pool 10 / threshold 5 at f1 0.5322, precision 0.3810, recall 0.8828 — i.e. no configuration in the sweep pairs threshold 5 with F1 0.552. The human-readable sibling at that era (git show a371376c1:results/h11-384-single-pass-t0-rerun/consensus-analysis-summary.md, '## Per-Temperature Optima' row 'brief-text-t0 | 10 | 10 | 0.5521') states the optimum as 10-of-10 unambiguously, so the defect is not inherited from a defective summary. Correct reading: '10-of-10'.
families.era_evidence: The anchor JSON has exactly one commit in its history — a371376c1 (2026-03-26), the same day the document was authored (8b596c00d, 2026-03-26) — and `git diff a371376c1 HEAD -- results/h11-384-single-pass-t0-rerun/` shows the only later change in that directory is one line of first-N boilerplate in consensus-analysis-summary.md (commit 1844e5887, 2026-07-28). The optima and results blocks are byte-stable across the document's entire lifetime, so era-state equals current state and the claim was wrong when written.
families.materiality: Moderate-low. The F1 value and pool size are correct; the misstated numeral is the operating point of the deterministic H11 baseline, which § 9 explicitly offers as 'the deterministic baseline for the tile-size comparison (H11)'. Anyone re-using the stated operating point would take 5-of-10 (F1 0.5322) instead of the reported optimum.

families.name: F2 — results-summary-session-58 § 11: cross-modal table denominator (572) matches no reference-mound population at any era
families.mechanism: Line 348 header reads '| Proposer pool | Matched refs | % of 572 |'. The anchor inputs/vectors/references/mounds-reference.geojson holds 569 features. The document's OWN preamble (line 17) states 'the full evaluation area (487 tiles, 569 reference mounds)', so the document contradicts itself at its own era. The table's percentage column is arithmetically derived from 572, not 569, confirming 572 is the operative denominator and not a typo confined to the header: 419/572 = 73.25 % (printed 73.3 %; on 569 it would be 73.6 %), 383/572 = 66.96 % (printed 67.0 %; on 569, 67.3 %), 421/572 = 73.60 % (printed 73.6 %; on 569, 74.0 %), 2/572 = 0.35 % (printed 0.3 %; on 569 it rounds to 0.4 %). Provenance of the stray 572: it is the candidate count of the proposer-verifier-384 pool, attested across era artefacts — results/h11-tile-size-results.md:284-289 ('572 candidates' on six rows), results/passes-manifest.md:134-139 (six proposer-verifier-384 passes, 572 each), reports/phase3a-verifier-completeness-audit-2026-05-03.md:529 ('572 expected'). The author appears to have substituted a candidate-pool size for the reference-mound total.
families.era_evidence: inputs/vectors/references/mounds-reference.geojson has a single commit in its history, cfc10c133 (2026-01-09), ten weeks before the document; it held 569 features then and holds 569 now (its four per-map siblings sum to 569: 136 + 217 + 196 + 20). `git diff 69e9cf748 HEAD -- reports/results-summary-session-58.md` shows the only post-March change to the document is the 2026-08-02 E72 superseded-figures banner; the § 11 table and the line-17 preamble are as written in March.
families.materiality: Moderate, and larger than the 572-vs-569 gap alone suggests. Independent recomputation (geopandas, inputs/vectors/references/mounds-reference.geojson within inputs/vectors/bounds/384/full_evaluation_bounds.geojson, 487 bound polygons) gives 435 reference mounds inside the 487-tile evaluation scope, not 569. Cross-check that 435 is the population the era's scorers actually used: results/verifier-robustness evals imply the same denominator (verified-adv-text-pro-vf-4of5, n_detections 393, precision 0.9262 -> 364 TP, recall 0.8368 -> 435; verified-adv-text-4of5, 389 and 0.9152 -> 356 TP, 0.8184 -> 435). So the § 11 percentage column rests on a denominator that matches neither the full reference set (569) nor the in-scope population (435). Any repair note should say so rather than simply substituting 569 for 572.

families.name: F3 — results-summary-session-58 Appendix A rows 377/378: anchor binds a different verifier probability-threshold operating point
families.mechanism: The document reports these two Appendix A cells at their own sweep argmax, and states that argmax explicitly: § 1c (lines 124-140) tabulates 'Medium | 0.859 | 0.878 | 0.841 | t=0.95' and 'HIGH | 0.853 | 0.867 | 0.839 | t=0.95', with the prose 'minimal peaks at t=0.15, while medium and HIGH peak at t=0.95' (lines 135-140). The extraction bound both rows to results/conditions-manifest.json cells whose registered probability thresholds are DIFFERENT operating points: pv-diag-384::verified-adv-text-medium-vf-4of5 carries prob_threshold 0.25, and pv-diag-384::verified-adv-text-high-vf-4of5 carries prob_threshold 0.5. The extraction note records the pool, verifier, n_passes and vote_threshold it matched on, and never mentions prob_threshold — the mis-binding is exactly rule 3 (locator denotes a different set from the one the prose asserts). Why the manifest holds no t=0.95 cell: the June re-derivation that produced these cells swept a capped grid — scripts/score_high_thinking_prior.py:63 defines PROB_TS = [0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5], and its output results/verifier-robustness/high_thinking_prior.log (header '=== THINKING axis at T=0.0 (>=3of5 band, best F1@20m over prob_t) ===') reports the 4of5 row as minimal_n1 0.8659, medium_n1 0.8545, high_n1 0.8519 — the recompute 'actual' values exactly. results/verifier-robustness/unswept_pools_sweep.json states the same grid in its method field ('proposer-k x prob_t {0.05..0.5}'). Both triples are internally consistent within their own evaluation (document: 2*0.878*0.841/(0.878+0.841) = 0.8591; manifest: 2*0.8656*0.8437/(0.8656+0.8437) = 0.8545), so the two numbers describe two different operating points of the same nominal condition, not a discrepancy in one of them. No document defect is established. Corroboration that these are the same conditions: results/run-analyses.json (analysis verifier-robustness-matrix) lists pv-diag-384::verified-adv-text-high-vf-4of5 as the 'single-pass HIGH-thinking prior' at 0.8519, and matrix_tiering.json's high-T0.0 entry gives its operating point as '4of5/mean/pt0.5'.
families.era_evidence: The anchor postdates the document by roughly two and a half months and could not have been resolved at the document's era: results/conditions-manifest.json's oldest commit in `git log` is 2026-05-30 (df26d543e), and the two underlying evaluations were committed 2026-06-10 (17c7e87ac, then 97d26256f). The document body dates from 2026-03-26/28 (8b596c00d, 69e9cf748). NOTE ON THE HARNESS era_check FIELD: for all batch-049 rows it reports commit a6f58d1b7604, which is the 2026-08-02 banner commit — the last commit to TOUCH the file, not the commit that authored the claims. Resolving 'the era' there yields the current artefact state, so era_check's 'faithful: false / actual_era == actual' on these rows carries no era information at all. It does not change my verdicts (F1 and F2 have era-stable anchors that I checked independently), but it is a real instrument limitation, recorded under recommendations.
families.residual: Era-faithfulness of the March figures cannot be tested at the artefact level: no March-era sweep for a Flash-HIGH-text pool under a Flash medium or Flash HIGH verifier exists in the tracked tree (`git ls-tree -r 69e9cf748 | grep verifier` under results/ yields only flash-minimal-*, pro-text-* and pro-image-* verifier directories). The document is internally consistent across § 1a, § 1b, § 1c and Appendix A, and its era sweep grid demonstrably ran to 0.95 (every era threshold_sweep_summary.md under results/h11-384-pv-diagnostic/ carries a 0.95 row), but 'no defect established' is the honest ceiling, not 'confirmed faithful'.

families.name: F4 — results-summary-session-58 Appendix A row 382: same operating point, later re-derivation over a re-materialised pool
families.mechanism: Unlike F3, the operating point is NOT mis-bound here: § 1a line 84 gives 'Pro HIGH image + Pro vf | 0.707 | 3-of-5, t=0.05 | 0.710 | 0.703', and the anchored manifest cell pv-diag-384::verified-adv-pro-image-pro-vf-3of5 carries vote_threshold 3 and prob_threshold 0.05 — the same nominal configuration. The divergence is a re-derivation difference. The current values come from results/verifier-robustness/unswept_pools_sweep.json (generated 2026-06-11T06:33:29Z), cell 'pro-high-image-5pass + pro vf' over an 841-candidate union, best_op '3of5/pt0.05', f1_20m 0.7112, precision_20m 0.712, recall_20m 0.7103, n_accepted 434; these were then materialised and re-scored into results/verifier-robustness/evals/verified-adv-pro-image-pro-vf-3of5/evaluation.json (2026-06-12, scripts/evaluate_detections.py, ground truth mounds-reference.geojson, bounds 384 full_evaluation_bounds, n_detections 434) and lifted into the manifest. Arithmetic on the two triples against the in-scope reference population of 435: June accepts 434 with 309 matches (0.712 * 434 = 309.0; 309/435 = 0.7103); the document's rounded triple implies 431 accepted with 306 matches (precision in [0.7095, 0.7105] and recall in [0.7025, 0.7035] force TP = 306 and n_accepted = 431). The acceptance sets therefore differ by three candidates, all matching. I tested and REJECTED the obvious boundary explanation (>= vs > at prob_t 0.05): the verifier probability distribution in outputs/h11/pv-diag-384/verified/pro-high-image-1of5-pro-verifier/probabilities.json holds 841 results with values {0.95: 642, 0.0: 117, 1.0: 57, 0.1: 10, 0.99: 5, 0.9: 4, 0.98: 4, 0.4: 1, 0.8: 1} — no candidate sits at exactly 0.05, so the threshold-comparison rule cannot move three candidates. The residual difference is attributable to the pool/scorer generation, not to the stated operating point.
families.era_evidence: Anchor artefacts postdate the document: the evaluation directory results/verifier-robustness/evals/verified-adv-pro-image-pro-vf-3of5/ has a single commit, dfdb74c6a (2026-06-12, '14-buffer evals for the 16 promoted sweep cells'); the sweep record is dated 2026-06-11; conditions-manifest.json did not exist before 2026-05-30. No March-era artefact for this cell exists in the tracked tree — results/h11-384-pv-diagnostic at 69e9cf748 contains pro-high-text-1of5..5of5 but no pro-high-image band directories — and the untracked-then-committed on-disk sibling outputs/h11/pv-diag-384/verified/pro-high-image-pro-vf-3of5/ carries a filesystem mtime of 2026-05-21, also post-dating the document. Era-faithfulness is therefore untestable; the anchor moved (was in fact created) after the document, which is the definition of snapshot divergence under ruling 14.
families.materiality: Low. Delta F1 0.0042, delta precision 0.0020, delta recall 0.0073; the row is a floor cell in Appendix A (worst of eight) and no ranking or conclusion in the document turns on it.

families.name: F5 — anchor-population mismatch: the locator counts a different population from the one the prose names (rule 3)
families.mechanism: One mechanism, three instances; in each the source document is correct and the locator resolves a different population. (a) 051#1[0] — reports/session-113-signoff-package.md:17 says 'thinking x temperature one tier at N=5; high hurts n=1'. The locator len:$.tiers over results/verifier-robustness/matrix_tiering.json returns 2 because the tiering board contains six configs, of which the second tier is exactly the n=1 single-pass HIGH prior the same sentence separately calls out: tiers = [[high-T0.3, min-T0.3, high-T0.7, min-T0.0, min-T0.7], [high-T0.0]]. Restricting $.ranked to the five N=5 refs (dropping high-T0.0) yields exactly one distinct tier — the prose's claim, verified. results/verifier-robustness/matrix_tiering.log confirms the composition ('FDR: 5/15 pairs significant at q=0.05 -> 2 tier(s)'; 'all 5 significant pairs involve high-T0.0'), as does results/run-analyses.json's verifier-robustness-matrix outcome: 'ALL FIVE N=5 configs are ONE statistical tier ... Only the single-pass HIGH-thinking prior drops to Tier 2 (0.8519)'. Locator is BROADER than the prose. (b) 056#41[0] — reports/verification/drafts/errata-drafts-2026-07-29.md:468-471 spot-checks 'the phase3c track-1 H9-A run-1 pool (4 954 detections)'. The extraction (which records that it never read the feature count) bound this to the single file outputs/retest/phase3c/track1-image/h9-A-p1/run_1/detections_h9-A-p1_run01.geojson = 1,032 features. The prose's pool is run 1 of ALL FIVE H9-A prompt arms: h9-A-p1..p5 run_1 together hold exactly 4,954 features, and the subtype tally over that union reproduces every reported share — burial_mound 4,102 = 82.8 %, benchmark_mound 501 = 10.1 %, triangulation_mound 316 = 6.4 %, settlement_mound 35 = 0.7 %, non-burial 852/4954 = 17.2 %, which is the exact figure the draft's own drafting note quotes ('My independent spot-check on a phase3c pool gives 17.2 %'). The single-arm file the extraction picked gives 83.4 / 9.6 / 6.4 / 0.6 — none of the document's figures. Locator is NARROWER than the prose. (c) 058#38[0] — reports/verification/family-fdr-registration.md:290 writes 'comparisons[0].p_value_adj (existing 26-row family)'. len:$.comparisons over results/pairwise/20m/fdr/pairwise_results_fdr.json returns 32, but the file splits 26 confirmatory + 6 exploratory on comparisons[i].family, and 'family' in an FDR context is precisely the correction unit. The same document states this explicitly in its own § 8.4 verification table (line 878 'total rows | 32 | metadata.n_comparisons'; line 879 'confirmatory rows | 26 | comparisons[i].family == "confirmatory"'; line 880 'exploratory rows | 6'), and re-derives the within-family arithmetic (line ~890: 'comparisons[29].p_value_raw = 0.0375 -> p_value_adj = 0.0488 = 0.0375 x 26/20'). Locator is BROADER than the prose.
families.era_evidence: All three anchors are era-stable, so no snapshot dimension exists for any of them. matrix_tiering.json: single commit 88a49e077 (2026-06-10), one day BEFORE the sign-off package was written (f02d703a8, 2026-06-11; last touched 96c9bd39c, 2026-06-12) — and the corroborating run-analyses.json outcome text is present verbatim in the blob at the document's own era commit 96c9bd39c. The five h9-A run_1 geojsons: all committed once, 3d22184d6 (2026-04-15), unchanged since — three and a half months before the 2026-07-29 draft (committed b68462bd8, 2026-07-30). pairwise_results_fdr.json: single commit 5d97d118c (2026-03-28), four months before the registration.

row_level_exceptions.note: REGISTRATION-INTEGRITY CHECK — RUN AND CLEARED, NOT ESCALATED. The brief flagged that post-registration growth of a registered family would be registration-integrity material. It did not occur. results/pairwise/20m/fdr/pairwise_results_fdr.json has exactly one commit in its entire history, 5d97d118c (2026-03-28), i.e. it has been byte-stable since four months BEFORE the registration commit 1dfff8130 (2026-07-30, 'REGISTER the family-FDR correction — committed before compute'). Its metadata.n_comparisons has read 32 throughout, and its confirmatory subset has been 26 throughout. The registration document itself records both counts in § 8.4 and warns that 'the 26-row family is not a superset of the seven primaries' (line 899). The 26-vs-32 gap is a locator artefact, not family growth; nothing about the registered family changed after the register was committed. `git diff 1dfff8130 HEAD -- reports/verification/family-fdr-registration.md` is +13/-1 lines and leaves line 290 untouched (the string 'existing 26-row family' is at line 290 in both blobs).

Direction of the population error is opposite to the other two members of family F5 (locator narrower, not broader). Grouped anyway because the mechanism — locator population != prose population, with the document correct — is identical, and the corrected anchor is a tracked five-file set (all five verified tracked via `git ls-files --error-unmatch`), so the claim is fully mechanical once re-bound.

The two sibling values in the same claim (049#2[0] F1 0.5521, 049#2[2] pool_size 10) both MATCH. The defect is isolated to a single numeral, which is why it survived authorship: '5' is a legal member of the sweep's pool_sizes list [5, 10] and reads plausibly in 'x-of-10' form.

The extraction flagged the internal inconsistency in its own note ('this document's own preamble at line 17 ... states 569 reference mounds') and correctly declined to adjudicate under instrument rule 4. The extraction is sound; the document is not. This is the one row in the partition where the extractor's doubt flag anticipated the verdict.

Ruling-15 exposure: there is NO cell anywhere in results/conditions-manifest.json at the document's operating point (prob_threshold 0.95) for either condition, because the registration sweep grid stops at 0.5. Re-binding cannot fix these rows — they are unanchorable in the current registry and belong in the NAMED 'anchored to neither' family rather than being carried as mechanical MISMATCHes.

recommendations.kind: append-only banner addendum (ruling 1 + ruling 14: dated session record, body unchanged)
recommendations.text: Append a second dated bullet BELOW the existing 2026-08-02 E72 banner — do not rewrite that banner. Content: (i) § 9's '5-of-10' should read '10-of-10'; the sweep's global optimum is threshold 10 of pool 10 at F1 0.5521 (results/h11-384-single-pass-t0-rerun/consensus-analysis-report.json, unchanged since commit a371376c1); 5-of-10 scores F1 0.5322. (ii) § 11's '% of 572' denominator matches no reference-mound population: the reference set held 569 features at the document's era and holds 569 now (inputs/vectors/references/mounds-reference.geojson, single commit cfc10c133), the document's own line 17 says 569, and the population actually inside the 487-tile evaluation bounds is 435 — so the percentage column should be treated as uncited rather than simply rescaled to 569. (iii) Appendix A rows 377/378 (Flash medium and Flash HIGH verifiers) report the t=0.95 optimum; the registered manifest cells for the same conditions are constrained-grid selections at prob_t 0.25 and 0.5 and are NOT the same operating point — cite one or the other, never interchangeably.

051#1[0]: replace len:$.tiers with a tier count restricted to the five N=5 refs — e.g. |{r.tier for r in $.ranked if r.ref != 'high-T0.0'}| = 1 — matching the prose's 'at N=5'. 056#41[0]: replace the single-file anchor with the five tracked files outputs/retest/phase3c/track1-image/h9-A-p{1,2,3,4,5}/run_1/detections_h9-A-p{n}_run01.geojson (sum of len:$.features = 4954; the four subtype shares and the ~17 % roll-up then all reproduce). 058#38[0]: replace len:$.comparisons with len([c for c in $.comparisons if c.family == 'confirmatory']) = 26. All three re-binds resolve against era-stable, git-tracked artefacts and should return the rows to MATCH.

recommendations.kind: instrument finding — recommend a registered fix, not a row status change
recommendations.text: For every batch-049 row the era_check field reports commit a6f58d1b7604, which is the 2026-08-02 banner commit — the last commit that TOUCHED the document, not the commit that authored the claim (the § 9, § 11 and Appendix A text is unchanged since 69e9cf748, 2026-03-28). Resolving anchors there is equivalent to resolving them at HEAD, so era_check contributed no era information on nine of my eleven batch-049 rows and reported 'faithful: false' on three rows (049#25, #26, #30) whose anchors did not exist in any form at the document's true era. Recommended: resolve the era commit as the last commit that changed the CLAIM'S OWN LINE RANGE (git log -L or a blame over source_lines), and emit an explicit 'anchor-absent-at-era' status when the anchor path has no blob at that commit, rather than silently falling through to the current artefact. Ruling 12 created this field precisely to separate SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE from defect mechanically; on banner-amended snapshots it currently does the opposite.

recommendations.target: results-summary-session-58 § 11 scope question (out of my partition, flagged for the PI queue)
recommendations.text: Independent recomputation puts 435 reference mounds inside inputs/vectors/bounds/384/full_evaluation_bounds.geojson (487 tiles), against 569 in the full reference set — and 435 is the denominator the era's own scorers used (recoverable from any pv-diag-384 evaluation's precision/recall/n_detections triple). The document's line-17 framing '(487 tiles, 569 reference mounds)' therefore conflates full-corpus GT with in-bounds GT. That framing is quoted well beyond § 11 and beyond this document; it is a separate, larger question than the 572 defect and I have not adjudicated it.
